# Consultation Security and Lifecycle Checklist: Doctor Consultation Lifecycle

**Purpose**: Deep PR-review checklist for the quality, completeness, clarity, and consistency of consultation lifecycle, authorization, concurrency, audit, recovery, timezone, and upstream-contract requirements.
**Created**: 2026-08-24
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are all permitted lifecycle states and every prohibited transition explicitly defined, including the standard invalid-state outcome? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK002 Are role, doctor-assignment, hospital, and branch requirements defined separately for call, start, and complete actions? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002–004, FR-007, FR-012]
- [ ] CHK003 Is the sole authoritative creation path for `WAITING` consultations defined together with the prohibition on direct creation? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK004 Are consultation-to-patient, doctor, hospital, branch, and source queue-entry relationships specified with sufficient uniqueness and ownership rules? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010; Data Model §Consultation]
- [ ] CHK005 Are requirements defined for all required lifecycle timing fields, their write points, and their retention after completion? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003–005; Data Model §Consultation]

## Authorization and Privacy Clarity

- [ ] CHK006 Is “authorized reception staff” defined by a precise trusted role and authorized hospital/branch scope rather than a request-provided attribute? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, FR-007–008, FR-012]
- [ ] CHK007 Is “assigned doctor” defined so the requirement unambiguously distinguishes doctor identity/assignment from a general clinical role? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003–004, FR-012]
- [ ] CHK008 Are production fail-closed behavior and the strictly test-only trusted staff context clearly separated, including safeguards against treating the latter as production authentication? [Security, Spec §FR-007–008, Assumptions; Plan §Technical Context]
- [ ] CHK009 Are non-disclosure requirements consistent for unknown, out-of-scope, wrong-role, and wrong-assignment lifecycle requests? [Consistency, Spec §Edge Cases, FR-007–008; Contract §Error and Idempotency Semantics]
- [ ] CHK010 Is the lifecycle response data boundary explicit enough to exclude patient contact details, clinical content, and unnecessary staff identity data? [Privacy, Contract §Lifecycle View]

## State, Concurrency, and Timing Consistency

- [ ] CHK011 Are the lifecycle order in the specification, data model, and API contract consistent with no missing, skipped, or conflicting state? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001; Data Model §Allowed State Transitions; Contract §§Call Patient–Complete Consultation]
- [ ] CHK012 Are duplicate and concurrent call, start, and complete outcomes specified consistently as one persisted transition with a non-mutating conflict for the loser? [Completeness, Spec §Acceptance Scenarios, FR-002–004, SC-002]
- [ ] CHK013 Is the concurrency rule explicit about the authoritative version/transaction boundary rather than relying only on an application-level precondition? [Clarity, Plan §Technical Context; Research §Guarded compare-and-set updates]
- [ ] CHK014 Are the actual start/end requirements precise about instants, ordering, and the behavior if timing persistence cannot be completed? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003–005, FR-011]
- [ ] CHK015 Are branch-timezone requirements limited to display/operational calculations and consistent with instant storage? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005, Edge Cases; Research §Store lifecycle times]

## Audit and Recovery Requirements

- [ ] CHK016 Are call, start, and completion audit requirements defined with action, prior/next state, trusted actor, scope, and PII-minimization expectations? [Completeness, Spec §FR-009; Data Model §Consultation Transition Audit]
- [ ] CHK017 Is the mandatory-audit failure outcome defined so no successful lifecycle transition is visible without its required audit record? [Recovery, Spec §FR-009, FR-011]
- [ ] CHK018 Is the completion consistency boundary explicit about state, end time, audit, and queue-recalculation hand-off rather than allowing partial success? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006, FR-011; Research §Consistency boundary]
- [ ] CHK019 Are recovery ownership, idempotency, retry limits, and terminal-failure visibility specified for a queued recalculation hand-off? [Gap, Data Model §Queue Recalculation Outbox; Plan §Post-design]
- [ ] CHK020 Are requirements defined for what staff can see or do when recalculation is pending recovery, rather than implying that estimates are already refreshed? [Gap, Spec §FR-006, SC-005]

## Upstream Contract and Dependency Coverage

- [ ] CHK021 Are the minimum check-in queue-entry contract fields and eligibility guarantees documented so consultation can validate its sole `WAITING` source without accessing upstream persistence? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013; Data Model §External Contract Relationships]
- [ ] CHK022 Is the queue-recalculation contract explicit about scope, event payload, acknowledgement, and idempotency key? [Gap, Spec §FR-006; Data Model §Queue Recalculation Outbox]
- [ ] CHK023 Are trusted identity contract requirements explicit about role semantics, authorized branch/hospital scope, and assigned-doctor identity? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007–008, FR-012; Research §Trusted staff-context port]
- [ ] CHK024 Are branch-timezone dependency requirements explicit about the authoritative source and behavior when it is unavailable or invalid? [Gap, Spec §FR-005; Plan §Integration prerequisite]
- [ ] CHK025 Are migration sequencing requirements defined against the integrated upstream schema baseline rather than an assumed local migration number? [Completeness, Plan §Project Structure, §Structure Decision]

## Acceptance and Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK026 Do acceptance scenarios cover the full successful receptionist-call and assigned-doctor start/complete sequence without conflating their authorities? [Coverage, Spec §User Stories 1–3]
- [ ] CHK027 Are invalid transition scenarios defined for every lifecycle action, including timestamp, audit, and queue non-mutation guarantees? [Coverage, Spec §User Stories 1–3, FR-001, FR-011]
- [ ] CHK028 Are wrong-role, wrong-branch, wrong-hospital, and wrong-assigned-doctor scenarios individually covered or intentionally grouped with equivalent non-disclosure semantics? [Coverage, Spec §FR-007–008, FR-012, SC-004]
- [ ] CHK029 Are concurrent state-mutation scenarios defined for the same consultation and for conflicting active consultations from the same source queue entry? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, SC-002; Data Model §Consultation]
- [ ] CHK030 Are recovery and failure-injection scenarios defined for audit persistence, queue hand-off persistence, delivery failure, and retry duplication? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 3, FR-011, SC-005]

## Measurability and Cross-Artifact Traceability

- [ ] CHK031 Are the success criteria objectively measurable with stated fixture assumptions, concurrency levels, measurement boundaries, and pass/fail rules where timing or recovery is claimed? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001–005; Plan §Performance Goals]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`.
